:::{#exr-rss-hessian-vector}
#### Hessian of RSS in vector notation

Find the [Hessian](intro-MLEs.qmd#def-hessian)
$\deriv{\vcoef} \deriv{\tp{\vcoef}} \text{RSS}(\vcoef)$,
and show that it is positive definite when $S_{xx} > 0$ (@def-centered-sums).
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-rss-hessian-vector}

Differentiate the gradient $-2 \paren{\v{c} - A \vcoef}$
from @exr-normal-equations-vector
with respect to $\tp{\vcoef}$.
$\v{c}$ does not depend on $\vcoef$.
Each entry of $A \vcoef$ is the dot product of a row of $A$ with $\vcoef$,
so by the gradient of a linear function
(@exr-rss-gradient-vector),
the derivative of $A \vcoef$ with respect to $\tp{\vcoef}$ is $A$.
So:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\deriv{\vcoef} \deriv{\tp{\vcoef}} \text{RSS}(\vcoef)
&= \deriv{\tp{\vcoef}} \paren{-2 \paren{\v{c} - A \vcoef}}
&& \text{(differentiate the gradient)}\\
&= -2 \deriv{\tp{\vcoef}} \paren{\v{c} - A \vcoef}
&& \text{(constant factor)}\\
&= -2 \paren{\deriv{\tp{\vcoef}} \v{c} - \deriv{\tp{\vcoef}} A \vcoef}
&& \text{(derivative of a difference)}\\
&= -2 \paren{\mat{0} - \deriv{\tp{\vcoef}} A \vcoef}
&& \text{($\v{c}$ does not depend on $\vcoef$)}\\
&= -2 \paren{\mat{0} - A}
&& \text{(derivative of a linear function)}\\
&= -2 \paren{-A}
&& \text{(subtract from zero)}\\
&= 2 A
&& \text{(multiply)}\\
&= 2 \sumin \soprod{\vxi}
&& \text{(definition of $A$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

To show it is positive definite,
take any vector $\v{v} = \tp{(v_0, v_x)} \neq \vzero$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\tp{\v{v}} \paren{2 A} \v{v}
&= 2 \, \tp{\v{v}} A \v{v}
&& \text{(constant factor)}\\
&= 2 \, \tp{\v{v}} \paren{\sumin \soprod{\vxi}} \v{v}
&& \text{(definition of $A$)}\\
&= 2 \sumin \tp{\v{v}} \paren{\soprod{\vxi}} \v{v}
&& \text{(matrix multiplication distributes over the sum)}\\
&= 2 \sumin \paren{\tprod{\v{v}}{\vxi}} \paren{\tprod{\vxi}{\v{v}}}
&& \text{(matrix multiplication is associative)}\\
&= 2 \sumin \paren{\dprod{\v{v}}{\vxi}} \paren{\dprod{\vxi}{\v{v}}}
&& \text{(transpose products as dot products)}\\
&= 2 \sumin \paren{\dprod{\v{v}}{\vxi}}^2
&& \text{(dot product is symmetric)}\\
&= 2 \sumin \paren{v_0 + v_x x_i}^2
&& \text{(write out the dot product)}\\
&\ge 0
&& \text{(sum of squares)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Equality would need $v_0 + v_x x_i = 0$ for every $i$.
If $v_x \neq 0$, that would force every $x_i = -v_0 / v_x$,
contradicting $S_{xx} > 0$;
if $v_x = 0$, it would force $v_0 = 0$,
contradicting $\v{v} \neq \vzero$.
So the inequality is strict,
and the Hessian is positive definite at every $\vcoef$.

:::
